newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece's Sunday election at a glance.
newsitem.headline: Greece's Sunday election at a glance.

text.p: Facts and figures on Greece, a member of the European Union and NATO, which went to the polls on Sunday to elect its next government:

- A 300-seat parliament is elected directly by the people every four years. The party that wins an absolute majority of parliamentary seats forms a government. The election was due in October 1997 but the socialist government of Prime Minister Costas Simitis called a snap poll citing national reasons. Simitis took over in January from an ailing Andreas Papandreou who died in June.

- There are 8,862,014 registered voters out of a population of just over 10 million. All citizens over 18 and under 70 must vote. The electoral system is reinforced proportional representation, which almost guarantees that the party with the largest vote will form a government.
- Parliament elects the head of state, now President Costis Stephanopoulos, every five years. The next such vote is due in the year 2000.

Polling stations opened at sunrise at 0413 GMT and will close at 1620 GMT.
